fields.summary: Add per-call rate limit on the public search endpoint
fields.description:
## Problem

WHAT: Anonymous callers hit `/v1/search` without any per-IP rate limit, which lets a single tenant exhaust the search node pool during peak hours.

WHY: Last week's incident (INC-1023) traced 88% of dropped requests to one IP. We need a deterministic per-IP cap so no single caller can degrade the rest of the tenant base.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Requests to `/v1/search` from a single IP beyond N/min (configurable, default 60) are rejected with HTTP 429 + a JSON body `{error: 'rate_limited', retry_after_seconds: <int>}`.
- AC2: Authenticated callers (any bearer token) bypass the per-IP cap and instead enforce the existing per-token quota.
- AC3: The limiter persists state in Redis so it survives pod restarts.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring the search node pool sizing.
- Tenant-tier-specific quotas (handled by the existing per-token quota).

## Target paths

- `services/search-api/src/middleware/`
- `services/search-api/src/config/`
- `services/search-api/tests/middleware/`

comments.body: LGTM on scope — please keep the default at 60/min.
